title: PART 2 - What Next Fest devs actually use AI for, from 2,443 Steam disclosures (only 5% name the tool)
author: Dream_Ep
selftext:
Yesterday I posted that 1 in 3 Next Fest games had an AI disclosure on their Steam page. Someone in the comments guessed it was mostly AI-assisted coding, which is a fair guess.. So I read them. All 2,443 ! ;)

Art, by far. 72% of disclosures mention it, and "art and nothing else" is the most common answer of all. Then translations (29%), writing (26%), the store page or trailer (26%), code (20%), music (19%), sound effects (18%) and voices (7%). A third of them list 3 uses or more !

So not really code.. Since January Valve doesn't even ask you to disclose AI coding tools, the form is about what players see or hear. Only about 1 in 10 disclosures (223) is just code, translation or the store page, with no AI art, sound or writing ! :D

Games with more followers use it differently. Under 50 followers, 19% mention music and 21% code. At 500 followers and up, music drops to 5%, and art to about half. Translation stays around 28% at every size, it's the one everybody's fine admitting. (Only 58 disclosing games above 500 followers, so rough numbers there.)

Some fun ones:

* Only 117 name the tool. Suno or Udio (38), Claude (31), ElevenLabs (30), ChatGPT (22), then Gemini, Midjourney and friends way behind.
* 52 promise the AI stuff is a placeholder that will be replaced.
* 67 make a point of saying their tools are licensed, "ethical", or trained on their own art.
* 53 generate content live while you play. Everyone else did it before shipping.
* Almost half say a human reviewed everything. And 315 said it all in 10 words or less, my favorite is just "Localization."

How I counted: keywords, sentence by sentence, so "no AI was used for the music" doesn't count as music. I read a sample by hand, it's right most of the time, the small categories are rougher. No game names..! I'm not here to display that in public ;)

Next one is the question everybody actually asks: did the label hurt these games during the fest? (Answer tomorrow ! )

I'm building NextWishlist, a tool that tracks this kind of stuff for your own game and its niche every day. Link in the comments if you're curious !!

comments.author: Dream_Ep
comments.body:
For the curious ones: I’m working on NextWishlist because most of us end up guessing whether our wishlists are “good” or not.

The idea is to see where your game stands in its niche, compared to games like yours, and get advice that actually fits your situation hehe

It’s a closed beta for now and I’m not selling anything, it’s free, I’m just looking for devs to test it and tell me what’s wrong with it. If that sounds useful to you, you can join the waitlist here: [https://nextwishlist.com](https://nextwishlist.com/?ref=igwai2) And if you’d just rather ask me questions, my DMs are open, happy to chat ! ;)

And since this whole thread is about it: yes, I use AI to build the site, like pretty much every dev in 2026. My actual job is data, not visuals. Collecting the Steam data, checking the numbers and trying to break my own results, that’s the part I do myself.. I'm building a tool that use that kind of data to help indie dev to market their game that's all !

comments.author: gamedevjp
comments.body: Love to see if disclosing hurt them. Looking forward to tomorrows post

replies.author: Dream_Ep
replies.body: Thanks! Tomorrow it is. Spoiler: I didn’t expect the answer either haha :D

comments.author: Masterkiefs
comments.body:
We only use it for code, no image gens.

In terms of the community, I felt it’s best to disclose it anyways rather than get bashed or reviewed bomb. 

I disclosed it honestly weather it’s required or not

replies.author: Dream_Ep
replies.body:
Respect for being upfront about it..!  
You’re actually in a small group: only about 1 in 10 disclosures (223) is just code, translation or the store page, with no AI art, sound or writing..  
Curious, did you get any reaction to it from players so far? ;)

comments.author: JBMorningstar
comments.body: If i ever release my game i'll just put "this game used AI in its production workflow" and leave it to interpretation how much it was

replies.author: Asexygentleman
replies.body: The problem is AI assets are very easy to spot. Your disclosure and the AI assets will result in nerd rage and subsequent negative review bombs.

replies.author: Dream_Ep
replies.body:
That’s the fear everyone has, and it’s exactly what tomorrow’s post is about. I compared follower growth during the fest between games of the same size, with and without the label. Short version: the label alone didn’t sink anyone, at least on followers.   
Reviews are another story though, most of these are unreleased demos, so I can’t measure that part yet

replies.author: Dream_Ep
replies.body:
Ha, you wouldn’t be alone. Only 117 of the 2,443 disclosures even name a tool, and a lot of them are one vague line !   
My favorite is literally just “Localization.” with a full stop, like a mic drop. Valve’s form does ask what the AI made, though, so super vague might not survive a review forever..! :D

comments.author: Creepy-Doughnut-5054
comments.body: coding even is something you are not obliged to disclose, so those who did fooked up

replies.author: Dream_Ep
replies.body:
True, since January Valve doesn’t ask for coding tools. But hardly anyone disclosed code alone. It usually shows up next to art, music or writing.   
Disclosures that only mention code, translation or the store page are about 1 in 10. And did they mess up? From what I saw in the growth numbers, not really, more on that tomorrow so stay tuned haha :D

comments.author: SeasawPhilosopher
comments.body: I only use free range grass fed AI in my games

replies.author: Dream_Ep
replies.body: You joke, but 67 disclosures really do insist their AI is licensed or “ethical”. Free range is the next logical step :D
